ClientBlockIn.description:
API 0.5 form: the tag was already programmed offline (ADR-0014).

`client_id` and `tag_token` are **both** required here. That is what makes the
two forms a closed choice rather than one model with optional halves: half an
identity can neither replay nor conflict, and a generator should refuse it
before a server has to.

It is **not** the canonical id: Service generates that and returns both. Two tenants may use the same value for unrelated blocks, and neither can learn anything about the other.

tag_token.description: The canonical ADR-0014 token: 32 random bytes as exactly 43 characters of unpadded base64url. Send the token only — never the whole `blocks://tag/v1/<token>` URI. A padded or standard-alphabet spelling of the same bytes is refused, because two spellings would hash differently and one physical tag would become two blocks. Service stores only the hash and **never returns this value**: you already hold it.

ClientRegisteredBlockOut.description:
Result of the API 0.5 client-supplied form.

**No `tag_token`, by construction.** You supplied it, so returning it would add
nothing — and it would not merely be displayed: idempotency persists a
response as JSON, so echoing the token would write the raw value into Service
storage, which is exactly what hashing it was for. `client_id` and the
canonical `id` are what a client needs to attribute the acknowledgement and
rewrite its dependent binding.

CloseOnExistingContinuation.description:
Close a session that was ALREADY parked, without inventing a tier.

A two-form union of "outcome" and "new continuation" would silently drop this
flow, and it is a real one: park at lunch, decide later the block is over.
Forcing such a client to re-send the continuation would duplicate the record;
forcing an `outcome_tier` would make it claim a tier it did not reach, which
invariant 8 rules out as firmly as invariant 3 rules out preserving nothing.

Explicit, so it cannot be produced by accident — an empty body still matches
no member. The server verifies a continuation actually exists and refuses
with `409` if it does not.

Close preserving an explicit continuation, atomically.

For the offline boundary: park and close as **one** operation, under the one
`If-Match` the client actually knows. Queuing park then close separately
cannot work offline — the park advances the row version, and the queued close
was written before that version existed.

No-result is `{"session": null, "parking": null}`, never `{}` and never an
omitted key. A generated client then has one shape to handle rather than

get.description: The authoritative re-entry surface. Returns, in order: the **active** session; otherwise the session owning the **globally newest non-superseded parking record**, whether parked or closed. State does not outrank recency — a parked session competes on the age of its own record like everything else. Constitution invariant 4 requires the newest parking record to be immediately available, so a client never reconstructs this. Both fields are required and nullable: no result is `{"session": null, "parking": null}`.

Append-only, so this is the whole truth: corrections appear as new records.

returns `404`. The distinction is the point — otherwise a stale id looks like
a session nobody has parked.
